Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Power Holdings, Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Power Holdings' Q2 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; John Hayes, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Strategy Officer; David Lee, Chief Technology Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Regulatory Officer; and Robert Kim, Chief Communications Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
1. Dividend policy and payout ratio strategy.
2. Investments in renewable energy and clean energy transition.
3. Capital expenditure plan and project updates.
4. Retirement of fossil fuel plants and replacement strategies.
5. Progress towards clean energy goals and emission reductions.
6. Storm response and recovery efforts.
7. Successful integration of our Lone Star Solar portfolio.
8. Advancement of our Net Zero 2040 program.

Let me provide some more detail on these eight key aspects. Sarah, over to you to walk us through the financial and strategic underpinnings here.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. For Q2, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.42, up 8% year-over-year, alongside adjusted funds from operations per share of $1.55. Let's start with our dividend policy and payout ratio strategy, which remains a key pillar of our shareholder value creation, consistently delivering returns for more than 25 years. We declared a quarterly dividend of $0.65 per share earlier this month—our 102nd consecutive payment and a 5% increase from last year. This equates to an annualized $2.60 per share, offering a yield of about 4.3% based on recent closes, outperforming the S&P 500 Utilities Index at 3.2% and aligning with leaders like Duke Energy and Southern Company. Over the last 10 years, our dividend has compounded at 5.2% annually, beating inflation thanks to rate base growth from $28 billion in 2014 to $42 billion now.

We target a 60-70% payout on GAAP EPS and even stronger coverage on AFFO. Trailing 12 months through Q2 showed 65% on EPS and 58% on AFFO, providing plenty of room for our $4.2 billion annual capex focused on grid hardening, renewables, and long-duration storage. Free cash flow covers dividends 1.9 times this year, improved from 1.7 times in 2023, aided by elevated ERCOT merchant prices and favorable Southeast rate cases. Industry averages hover at 65-75% per S&P Global, but clean energy capex has nudged it to 62% lately due to IRA incentives and FERC Order 2222 for distributed resources. Our ratio briefly hit 62% in 2022 after Texas Winter Storm Uri investments but has recovered with returns.

By region, Southeast regulated markets like Georgia, Carolinas, and Florida enjoy stable 9.5% ROEs and low weather risk, supporting 68% payouts; we have a $450 million rate base request pending in Georgia for CCUS natural gas peakers meeting EPA methane standards. In Texas, our 2.5 GW unregulated renewables generated $320 million in Q2 margins, up 25%, but payouts are conservative at 55% to fund 1 GW BESS by 2026 at 15% IRRs. We optimize via DRIP uptake of $45 million last year, $150 million YTD buybacks under $500 million authorization at 10% below book, and guide 6-7% dividend growth through 2027 backed by 5-6% EPS from $12 billion five-year capex: 40% renewables adding 3 GW solar-plus-storage, 30% transmission like HVDC for offshore wind, 20% nuclear extensions on 2 GW fleet, 10% VPPs with Stem and AutoGrid. We've earned an 'A' on S&P's dividend scorecard with 3.8x net debt/EBITDA, BBB+/Baa1 ratings, and stress tests show 1.5x FCF coverage even in net-zero volatility. Tailwinds like 15% peak demand growth by 2030 from EVs and data centers, plus FERC Order 1920, support this framework—no changes planned as we eye Dividend Aristocrat status by 2026.

Shifting to investments in renewable energy and clean energy transition, our portfolio is now 42% of capacity, up from 28% three years ago. Q2 capex hit $850 million toward clean projects, pacing to $3.2 billion or 55% of total capex. We added 750 MW utility-scale solar in ERCOT/SPP with bifacial PERC from First Solar/LONGi at 28%+ factors via trackers and DC-coupled batteries; 400 MW onshore wind in Midwest with GE Vernova 3.0-113 at 55% factors; 300 MW/1,200 MWh standalone BESS in California with Tesla Megapack for duck curve firming. Renewables output rose 22% to 12.5 TWh or 38% total, with new solar PPAs at $28/MWh LCOE $24/MWh, wind $32/MWh, IRRs 9-11%. R&D includes $500 million for Form Energy iron-air 100-hour storage in PJM, 20 MW electrolyzer for 50 tons/day green H2 with ITM Power blended at Texas gas plant, $200 million inverters/dynamic ratings from AutoGrid lifting Texas curtailment thresholds 15% at 35% penetration. U.S. regulated/competitive split hedges risk; Texas ancillaries $150 million; 25% Hornsea Three offshore stake COD Q4 at £41.61/MWh; India 500 MW solar at $0.22/W. 5.5 GW PPA backlog at $35/MWh with Google/Microsoft, $1.1 billion ITC/PTC monetized; raising 2025 capex to $3.8 billion for 8 GW adds, 50% clean share.

On our capital expenditure plan and project updates, we're holding 2024 guidance at $7.8 billion, up 12% YoY, with $5.9 billion deployed YTD and $220 million AFUDC. Five-year plan to 2028 is $42 billion, up 15%, for 10% rate base CAGR to $55 billion at >10% ROIC; 65% renewables/storage for 55 GW clean by 2030. Renewables: 650 MW Flagship Solar Georgia COD at $1.05/W with 26.5% factor; 1.2 GW Lone Star Wind+Storage ERCOT NTP Q1 2025; 1,100 MW Atlantic Horizon offshore 40% fabricated at $2.9M/MW with Vestas V236; 1.2 GWh storage YTD. T&D: $2.1 billion including $450 million Northeast HVDC, $320 million MISO reconductoring with 3M Zaplok +50% ratings, $150 million AMI 2.0 with Itron DERMS. Nuclear 93.2% factor, $800 million renewals; gas CCUS with MHI for 45Q. Supports 8.5-9% EPS growth amid EV/data center loads.

Regarding retirement of fossil fuel plants and replacement strategies, we retired 1.2 GW subcritical coal at Heartland Station Q2, YTD 2.8 GW or 18% fleet, on track for 5 GW coal by 2026 and 800 MW old peakers ERCOT. Coal LCOE $45-55/MWh vs solar-storage $28-32/MWh; avoided $150 million opex, +250 bps EBITDA. Replaced with 1.1 GW: 700 MW solar PJM/SPP +300 MW/1,200 MWh LFP BESS; 400 MW FlexHub wind+BESS ERCOT earning $45 million ancillaries. PJM 2 GW fast-track, PPAs $35/MWh; CAISO Sonoran 500 MW for RA. Merchant 40% in Texas data centers; CCUS on Permian NGCC; $2.5 billion capex for 4 GW adds. De-risks to 25% fossil by 2028, 8-10% FFO/share growth.

On progress toward clean energy goals and emission reductions, Scope 1/2 GHG down 18% YTD to 32.7 million tons vs 2019 base, ahead of 25% 2025 cut; coal <15%, renewables/zero-carbon 52% Q3 mix up from 42%. Added 1.2 GW solar ERCOT/PJM like 450 MW Desert Bloom 28% factor; 600 MW wind SPP; 750 MW/2.8 GWh BESS CAISO +$80 million ancillaries; 500 MW H2 electrolyzer pilot. Southeast 22% cut via 800 MW solar PPAs; ERCOT 30% down, $250 million uplift; MISO nuclear extensions; CAISO stacking. $12 billion capex 65% clean for 70% carbon-free 2030, net-zero 2045; $2.5 billion IRA credits, SMR with NuScale.

Finally, on storm response and recovery, we'll cover that in Q&A as analysts have asked, but high-level, we managed Hurricane Epsilon effectively with rapid restoration.

Alex Rivera: Excellent overview, Sarah—those initiatives position us strongly. Now, to the financials more broadly. Sarah?

Sarah Kline: Thank you, Alex. Good morning again. For Q2, earnings per share stood at $1.42 with revenue of $4.8 billion, showcasing our diversified model and capital discipline. Quarterly capex was $1.95 billion, focused on renewables and grid upgrades. We maintain a strong balance sheet, returning value via dividends and buybacks, and anticipate 6-9% EPS growth in FY2025.

Before detailing further, a reminder on forward-looking statements: Our FY2025 guidance for adjusted EBITDA $4.8-5.0 billion (7-10% growth), revenues $18.5-19.5 billion, EPS $4.85-5.05 (6-9% growth), capex $6.2-6.8 billion. Driven by 8% sales volume growth to 120,000 GWh from data centers, ERCOT margins +12-15% at $150/MWh peaks. To 2030, 8-10% EBITDA CAGR, 60% renewables, $25 billion capex: 10 GW solar/wind, 5 GWh storage, SMRs 1.2 GW, T&D $4 billion. Regulated ROE 10.5%, 70/30 contracted/merchant, risks mitigated via hedges, supply chains.

John Hayes: Thank you, Sarah. Operationally, efficiency in our combined cycle gas turbine plants improved via digital twin technology, yielding a 15% output increase. Outage rates dropped 25%.

Lisa Chen: Thanks, John. Strategically, we're pursuing battery storage opportunities, a future growth driver, and evaluating acquisitions in ERCOT.

David Lee: Thank you, Lisa. Technologically, investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity include our new AI-based threat detection system against cyber risks. We're piloting smart grid inverters in Texas.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, David. Regulatorily, approval for our rate case in PJM allows recovery of $500 million in capex.

Robert Kim: Thank you, Maria. Our outreach in Southeast Florida communities boosted positive sentiment by 20%.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, John, Lisa, David, Maria, and Robert. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Thank you. We'll now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning everyone. I wanted to dive into the storm response and recovery efforts, particularly around Hurricane Epsilon that hit our Southeast footprint late last quarter. Could you walk us through the financial impacts, restoration metrics, and any updates on your resiliency capex program? How does this tie into your updated FY guidance?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Sarah, and good morning. I'll start and turn to Sarah Kline for financials. Our teams shone during Category 3 Hurricane Epsilon, landfall near Florida/Georgia October 15, peaking at 1.47 million outages or 28% of 5.2 million customers, mainly Miami-Dade/Jacksonville. Up from 1.1 million in Delta last year per NOAA trends.

We deployed 12,000 personnel including 4,500 mutual aid from Duke, FPL, Southern within 24 hours; 65% restored by hour 24 vs 50% target, 99.8% by day 5 beating PSC benchmarks. SAIDI 145 minutes, 12% better than average via ADMS, 150 drones scanning 2,400 miles (85% damage ID), IBM Watson 92% outage forecast, AMI data. Accelerated 120 miles undergrounding South Florida -35% exposure.

Florida $180 million damages (70%), Georgia $65 million; lower than FPL via diversified mix, tree-trimming. Reinforces $2.8 billion 5-year resiliency: FRP poles, microgrids, VPP 150 MW dispatch. Rate filings for 85% recovery securitization.

Sarah Kline: Total O&M $285 million Q4 ($210 million restoration, $75 million aid), 8% over estimate on steel costs, but $195 million insurance/regulatory recovery (95% on $400 million policy), $45 million after-tax EPS hit ($0.12/share) in guidance. Recovery capex $420 million, 60% AFUDC for 10.2% ROE. Costs up 18% CAGR but 3:1 BCR, SAIFI 1.2 vs industry 1.8, NPS 78. No FY change at $3.45-3.55 EPS, capex $1.9 billion (25% resiliency), O&M +3%.

Sarah Jenkins, your line is open.

Operator: Next question from Julien Dumoulin-Smith with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Julien Dumoulin-Smith: Thanks, and congrats on a solid quarter, team. Just wanted to drill into the regulated capex guidance. You raised the 5-year capex to $12.5 billion from $11.2 billion last quarter—can you walk us through the drivers there, particularly around the battery storage queue and how you're thinking about AFUDC versus equity returns in this high-interest-rate environment?

Sarah Kline: Thanks, Julien. The $1.3 billion increase accelerates battery storage, with 1.2 GW queued in ERCOT/PJM vs 800 MW year-end '23, like 300 MW/1,200 MWh at King Mountain Wind Texas Q4 '25 COD for data center peaks (ERCOT +15% load). AFUDC at 7.8% via FERC NOPR; rate cases for 10.5% ROE citing risks. Supports 6-8% EPS CAGR, FFO/debt >18%.

Operator: Next question from David Arcaro with Morgan Stanley.

David Arcaro: Hey team, strong beat on adjusted EBITDA—up 12% YoY to $1.8 billion. But wholesale margins compressed 5% in the merchant fleet. With nat gas at $2.80/MMBtu and coal retirements accelerating, how are you hedging the gas fleet for '25, and any color on the forward curve shaping your dispatch stack versus peers like Vistra or Talen?

Alex Rivera: David, unregulated EBITDA $450 million Q2 record despite compression. 85% hedged '25 gas at $45/MWh vs NYMEX $42; 3.2 GW CC +1.8 GW peakers at 92% Q2 factor > Vistra ERCOT 88%. PJM DOM $38/MWh summer '25; 400 MW tolling PPAs negotiating $55/MWh data centers. Retiring 500 MW Big Stone coal '26 for 250 MW NuScale SMR, carbon <350 lbs/MWh pre-EPA.

Operator: Our next question is from Neal Dingmann with Oppenheimer.

Neal Dingmann: Congrats again. On the renewables side, solar curtailment in CAISO hit 8% in Q2—higher than the 6% we modeled. With your 2.5 GW pipeline, how are you mitigating that, and any updates on IRA PTC adders or storage co-locates to boost capacity factors?

Sarah Kline: Neal, CAISO 7.5% system-wide but our Imperial Valley 4.2% via 200 MW/800 MWh hybrid. Pipeline 70% co-located like 400 MW Gemini +1.6 GWh Fluence at 28-32% factors, 30% ITC adder. LCFS $15/MWh CA uplift, PPAs $35/MWh PG&E/SCE; Texas 95%+ utilization, 600 MW wind repowers GE 6.0 for +45% AEP.

Operator: And from Angie Storozynski with Seaport Global.

Angie Storozynski: Thanks. Dividend looks sustainable at 65% payout, but with $2.2 billion in '24 FCF guidance, what's the incremental allocation—buybacks, renewables M&A, or bolt-ons like the recent $300 million Sunnova deal? And color on Texas storm impacts?

Alex Rivera: Angie, 4.2% yield cornerstone, $1.48 quarterly 16x covered. FCF: 40% dividend, 30% debt paydown (3.5x target), 20% buybacks ($150 million YTD $52 avg), 10% tuck-ins. Sunnova JV 150 MW rooftop 12% IRR 70/30 split. Texas Winter Storm Prairie $45 million uninsured but SAIDI -95% via hardening, $20 million ERCOT ancillaries; 500 MW DR for '25.

Operator: Final question from Gregg Orrill with Barclays.

Gregg Orrill: Quick one on transmission. With FERC Order 1920 mandating long-term planning, how much of your $3.5 billion 5-year T&D capex is HVDC or reconductoring, and competitive dynamics with NextEra T&T?

Sarah Kline: Gregg, Order 1920 tailwind: $3.5 billion has $1.2 billion 345 kV reconductors PJM ACCC +50%, $800 million 500 kV HVDC MISO wind. Triennial scenarios 2-5 GW interregional. 15% T&D ROE like NextEra, Midwest ROW advantage; 1.5-2% rate base growth formula rates.

Operator: That concludes today's Q&A. There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q2 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Apex Power Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Apex Power Holdings.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
